messages:
maria: quick sync  we need a low-friction migration so API keys can carry route-level permissions without forcing mass rotations. idea: edge token-translator that emits short-lived signed leases.

jordan: are those leases stateless JWTs or opaque handles?

maria: prefer signed JWTs with minimal claims: routes (pattern ids), org_id, project_id, and role set. runtime can verify signature and avoid DB hits. TTL short (1-3m).

kevin: perf note: per-request signing will add p99. to reduce overhead we should cache translated token per (key, route_template) for short TTLs and use fast local signing worker pool.

oliver: what about revocation? stateless tokens are hard to revoke instantly.

maria: combine short TTL + invalidation pub/sub. edge keeps tiny in-memory invalidation set; on revoke we publish key id so edge can drop cached tokens. for high-security customers we provide stateful introspection so revoke is immediate.

security-bot: audit: 2026-03-10 long-lived keys still used by 32% of orgs. revocation propagation currently ~4-6m. :warning:

jordan: operational tradeoffs to document in RFC: opt-in per org, mapping table for audits (legacy_key -> active_leases), metrics (lease mint QPS, cache hit rate, revocation latency).

kevin: internal background jobs will be affected. propose "service-bound" tokens: long-lived but bound to instance identity (cert or instance id) and narrow role set to avoid per-request minting.

maria: include that flow as alternate path. also we should limit route claim granularity to templates not resource ids to avoid combinatorial token explosion.

devops: ops concerns: edge memory for invalidation, complexity of pub/sub, and key-signing throughput. need runbook for KMS scaling and fallback (offline sign queue).

maria: agreed. mitigation list for RFC: prefix-cache strategy, TTL ceiling (3m), key rotation plan, KMS worker pool with batching, and enterprise introspection endpoint.

jordan: i'll draft the RFC with sections: goals, threat model, token formats, caching strategy, revocation/invalidation, migration checklist, metrics/SLOs, runbook. kevin add perf numbers.

maria: i'll add example JWT payloads and a short migration checklist. target draft Wed EOD. tagging @devops for runbook review when ready. :+1:
